{{Quote|Yeah! Transport Away!|Derek "Hobbie" Klivian exclaims ''Thon's Orchard''{{'s}} escape from Hoth|<ref name="Running the Gauntlet-GG3-2" />}}
'''''Thon's Orchard''''' was a [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transport]] of the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Rebel Alliance Fleet]]. Originally a product of ill-fated [[Starship/Legends|starship]] manufacturer [[Gallofree Yards, Inc./Legends|Gallofree Yards]], which went bankrupt several [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the height of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], ''Thon's Orchard'' and other outdated Gallofree [[Transport/Legends|transports]] like it were sold to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] at bargain prices. As one of thirty GR-75 medium transports stationed at [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]], the [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] headquarters on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Water/Legends|ice]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], ''Thon's Orchard'' later helped facilitate the Rebellion's successful evacuation of its compromised outpost during the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].

The Rebels' defensive strategy against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] invasion [[Blizzard Force/Legends|force]] during the battle relied heavily on the Echo Base transport [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] to evacuate command personnel and supplies from the besieged planet. While the [[Rebel pilot/Legends|Rebel pilots]] of [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Group]] fought to buy [[Time/Legends|time]] for the evacuation, the transports faced a dangerous run through the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyer]] [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] in Hoth's [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]], with only minimal [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] escort and covering fire from Echo Base's [[V-150 Planet Defender/Legends|planetary ion cannon]] to protect them. ''Thon's Orchard'', [[Pilot/Legends|piloted]] by Rogue Group member [[Tarrin Datch/Legends|Tarrin Datch]], departed Echo Base with the final evacuation group late in the battle. Despite the loss of the [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]], ''Thon's Orchard'' safely passed through the Imperial blockade with assistance from escort pilots [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], and [[Derek Klivian/Legends|Derek "Hobbie" Klivian]] and regrouped with the Alliance at its [[Haven (rendezvous point)|rendezvous point]].

==Description==
''Thon's Orchard'' was a [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transport]] manufactured by [[Gallofree Yards, Inc./Legends|Gallofree Yards, Inc.]] that served in the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Rebel Alliance Fleet]]. The [[Transport/Legends|transport]] measured ninety [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length,<ref name="Complete Locations" /> was equipped with [[Sublight engine/Legends|sublight]] and [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] [[Engine/Legends|engines]], and its [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] contained a [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] for [[Starship/Legends|ship]]-to-ship communications.<ref name="Running the Gauntlet-GG3-2" />

==History==
===Battle of Hoth===
{{Dialogue|Antilles|This is the last evacuation group.|Skywalker|Hey, you should be gone already. How come you're still hanging around?|Antilles|Well, we sort of got delayed&mdash;a little bit of this.|Datch|Little of that.|Antilles|Yeah, while we were, uh&mdash;|Skywalker|While you were waiting for me. Thanks, guys.|attr=Wedge Antilles, Luke Skywalker, and Tarrin Datch|src=<ref name="ESB radio">{{ESBRadio|The Millennium Falcon Pursuit}}</ref>}}
Following starship manufacturer Gallofree Yards' bankruptcy several [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], many of the company's remaining transports ended up in the service of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]<ref name="CSWE-Gallofree">{{CSWECite|I|317|Gallofree Yards, Inc.}}</ref> in its [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|struggle]] against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The Rebellion purchased these<ref name="Complete Locations" /> outdated<ref name="NEGVV">''[[The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref> transports at bargain prices,<ref name="Complete Locations" /> but they nevertheless required plenty of regular upkeep.<ref name="RebelTransportDatabank" /> By the year [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="Complete Locations" /><ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the secret [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] headquarters of [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]], located on the remote [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Water/Legends|ice]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]],<ref name="Essential Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> housed a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of thirty GR-75 medium transports, including ''Thon's Orchard''.<ref name="Complete Locations" />

[[File:TransportsEchoBase-SWCL.png|thumb|left|350px|''Thon's Orchard'' (far right) and other Rebel transports stationed inside Echo Base early during the Battle of Hoth]]
The Empire's discovery of Echo Base in 3 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]] forced the Rebellion into a hasty evacuation of its compromised facility.<ref name="NEC" /> As Imperial [[Blizzard Force/Legends|forces]] descended on the base in the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], ''Thon's Orchard''<ref name="Complete Locations" /> and the rest of the transport fleet had the critical responsibility of evacuating command personnel and important supplies from the ice planet<ref name="RebelTransportDatabank" />&mdash;a difficult task that required each transport to pass through the Imperial [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] waiting in low Hoth [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] under minimal [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] escort and surface-to-[[Realspace/Legends|space]] covering fire from the base's [[V-150 Planet Defender/Legends|v-150 Planet Defender]] [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]]. The Echo Base defenses, meanwhile, had to [[Evac Rearguard Action 101|delay]] the Imperial invasion force as long as possible to give the transports [[Time/Legends|time]] to escape.<ref name="GG3, 2nd">[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'', Second Edition]]</ref>

Echo Base's transport fleet and its starfighter escorts began assembling at the Rebels' [[South Ridge/Legends|South Ridge]] evacuation launch site<ref name="Complete Locations" /> and lifted off one by one while the [[Ground warfare/Legends|battle]] raged.<ref name="CSWE-Hoth">{{CSWECite|II|62|Hoth, Battle of}}</ref> However, as the situation grew dire for the Rebels, base command ordered the transports to begin running the Imperial blockade in pairs, a risky prospect, as the Rebels could not guarantee that the base's ion [[Cannon/Legends|cannon]] could protect multiple transports at once.<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref> ''Thon's Orchard'' assembled at the staging area as part of the final evacuation group,<ref name="ESB radio" /> with [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Group]] member [[Tarrin Datch/Legends|Tarrin Datch]] set to [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] the transport on its blockade run,<ref name="Insider 146" /><ref name="GG3, 2nd" /> though Datch and fellow [[Rogue Three/Legends|Rogue]] [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] delayed ''Thon's Orchard''{{'s}} departure to wait for [[Rogue Leader/Legends|Rogue Leader]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], one of the last surviving [[Rebel pilot/Legends|pilots]] to reach the South Ridge.<ref name="ESB radio" />

Along with ''Thon's Orchard'', the final evacuation group included the GR-75 medium transports [[Dutyfree/Legends|''Dutyfree'']] and [[Bright Hope/Legends|''Bright Hope'']], escorted collectively by six [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing starfighters]], including pilots Skywalker, Antilles, and [[Tarn Mison]], as well as pilots [[Derek Klivian/Legends|Derek "Hobbie" Klivian]] and [[Wes Janson/Legends|Wes Janson]] flying together in a [[BTL-S3 Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL-S3 Y-wing starfighter]].<ref name="Note">This article concludes that the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|transports]] ''Thon's Orchard'', [[Dutyfree/Legends|''Dutyfree'']], and [[Bright Hope/Legends|''Bright Hope'']], as well as [[Rebel pilot/Legends|Rebel pilots]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], [[Derek Klivian/Legends|Derek Klivian]], [[Wes Janson/Legends|Wes Janson]], and [[Tarn Mison]], comprise the final evacuation group to depart [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], based on combined information from [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio drama]], ''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'', [[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'', Second Edition]], ''[[Tales of the Bounty Hunters]]'', {{CCG|set=Special Edition Limited|cardname=Lieutenant Tarn Mison}}, ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]'', and ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''. Please see this article's "Behind the scenes" section for a more detailed explanation.</ref> Rebel [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]] also rode aboard ''Thon's Orchard''.<ref name="GG3, 2nd" /> Knowing that Imperial [[Cold assault stormtrooper|snowtroopers]] had already seized control of the base and were bearing down on their position, the group lifted off with no time to spare.<ref name="ESB radio" /> However, complicating the group's blockade run, the Empire had also captured the ion cannon,<ref name="GG3, 2nd" /> eliminating any hope that the<ref name="Running the Gauntlet-GG3-2" /> transports<ref name="Note" /> would have protective fire as they braved the waiting Imperial [[Warship/Legends|warships]].<ref name="Running the Gauntlet-GG3-2" />

===Running the gauntlet===
{{Quote|Transport Commander, this is Leader One. Adjust to course 2-7-5.''"<br />"''What's the idea, boss? Why do you want him hangin' back like that?''"<br />"''Trust me.|Derek Klivian questions Wedge Antilles' order to ''Thon's Orchard''|<ref name="Running the Gauntlet-GG3-2" />}}
[[File:Last3Transports-RSIII.png|thumb|right|307px|Luke Skywalker escorts the transports ''Thon's Orchard'', ''Dutyfree'', and ''Bright Hope'' from Hoth.]]
''Thon's Orchard'', ''Dutyfree'', and the ''Bright Hope'' departed Echo Base as the last three transports to evacuate,<ref name="Note 2">The ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]'' level "[[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battlefield Hoth]]" depicts the last three [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|transports]] departing [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]]. This article concludes that these three [[Transport/Legends|transports]] are ''Thon's Orchard'', [[Dutyfree/Legends|''Dutyfree'']], and the [[Bright Hope/Legends|''Bright Hope'']], based on combined information from [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio drama]], [[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'', Second Edition]], ''[[Tales of the Bounty Hunters]]'', and ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''. Please see this article's "Behind the scenes" section for a more detailed explanation.</ref> but the group soon encountered large [[Squad/Legends|squads]]<ref name="Rebel Strike Player's Guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref> of incoming [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighters]], [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE interceptors]], and [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE bombers]] in Hoth's [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]. The [[Bomber/Legends|bombers]] harried each of the three transports, requiring Skywalker to [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dispatch]] many of the attacking Imperial fighters before they could destroy the fleeing Rebel cargo ships.<ref name="Rogue Squadron III">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref> Yet ''Thon's Orchard''{{'s}} path still was not clear&mdash;an [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyer]] sat directly in its escape lane as the transport entered Hoth's orbit.<ref name="Running the Gauntlet-GG3-2" />

With the [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] spitting heavy [[Laser/Legends|laser]] fire, Antilles ordered ''Thon's Orchard'' to drop back while he prepared to execute a radical maneuver, called the [[Tallon split]], designed to fool the [[Targeting computer/Legends|computer]]-controlled Imperial guns. By pulling his fighter close together with Derek Klivian's Y-wing, Antilles effectively tricked the Star Destroyer into reading their ships as a single target. Once they were close enough, they split their fighters apart, too quickly for the Star Destroyer to track them both at once, allowing Antilles a clear shot that destroyed one of the Star Destroyer's [[ISD-72x deflector shield generator dome|sensor globes]].<ref name="Running the Gauntlet-GG3-2" /> Their maneuver, combined with a hidden attack by Skywalker from underneath the transport, cleared the way for Datch and ''Thon's Orchard'' to escape into [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]].<ref name="Essential Guide to Characters">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref>

Skywalker, Antilles, Klivian,<ref name="GG3, 2nd" /><ref name="Essential Guide to Characters" /> Mison,<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=Special Edition Limited|cardname=Lieutenant Tarn Mison}}</ref><ref name="Of Possible Futures">{{StoryCite|story=Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref> and the ''Dutyfree'' similarly survived the blockade run,<ref name="Isard's Revenge">''[[X-Wing: Isard's Revenge]]''</ref> although the ''Bright Hope'' was destroyed.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" /> ''Thon's Orchard'' safely rejoined the Alliance Fleet at the Rebels' predetermined [[Haven (rendezvous point)|rendezvous point]]<ref name="GG3, 2nd" /> above the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] plane,<ref name="Essential Atlas" /> but it was among<ref name="Running the Gauntlet-GG3-2" /> just thirteen of Echo Base's thirty transports to avoid destruction in the Battle of Hoth, which proved to be a devastating Rebel defeat.<ref name="Complete Locations" /> Afterward, Antilles recorded ''Thon's Orchard''{{'s}} blockade run in his personal memoirs, which he shared with Voren Na'al for the latter's ongoing documentation work of the Rebel Alliance's history.<ref name="Running the Gauntlet-GG3-2" /><ref name="GG3, 2nd" />

==Commanders and crew==
During the Battle of Hoth, the [[Human/Legends|Human]] male Tarrin Datch successfully piloted ''Thon's Orchard'' past the Imperial Star Destroyer blockade<ref name="Insider 146" /> and regrouped with the rest of the Alliance Fleet at the rendezvous point. A member of Rogue Group as [[Rogue Ten/Legends|Rogue Ten]], Datch served dual piloting duty during the battle,<ref name="GG3, 2nd" /> also flying one of Echo Base's [[Snowspeeder/Legends|snowspeeders]] against the Imperial invasion force<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> before leading ''Thon's Orchard'' to safety.<ref name="GG3, 2nd" /> Datch knew Wedge Antilles well enough not to question his unorthodox order to adjust ''Thon's Orchard''{{'s}} course in preparation for Antilles' Tallon split maneuver, which helped the transport to evade the blockading Star Destroyer.<ref name="Running the Gauntlet-GG3-2" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Continuity development and inconsistencies===
''Thon's Orchard'' traces its origins to author [[Brian Daley]]'s [[1983]] [[National Public Radio]] [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|dramatization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']]. In the [[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization|unabridged script]] for the radio drama, Luke Skywalker and Wedge Antilles escort a Rebel transport, piloted by a character named Tarrin, away from Hoth. After lifting off, the pilots encounter a Star Destroyer. Skywalker orders Antilles to pull their fighters close together underneath the transport so that they will appear as a single blip on the Star Destroyer's [[Radar/Legends|radar]]. At the right moment, Skywalker orders Antilles to fire a [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedo]] at the Star Destroyer, a surprise attack that damages the Imperial ship enough to allow the transport to escape into hyperspace.<ref name="ESB radio script">[[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization|''The Empire Strikes Back'': The National Public Radio Dramatization]]</ref>

However, much of this dialogue was cut from the final recorded version of the radio episode, "[[The Millennium Falcon Pursuit|The ''Millennium Falcon'' Pursuit]]." In the episode, references to Tarrin's transport are removed, implying that he may be in a fighter like Luke and Wedge. The ships of the Imperial Starfleet have scattered in pursuit of other Rebels, so the three pilots are able to slip through the blockade without incident. Luke flies his fighter in the direction of two very distant Star Destroyers in case they "try something," but he is only using them as an excuse to separate from the other two pilots so that he can surreptitiously set course for the [[Dagobah system/Legends|Dagobah system]].<ref name="ESB radio" /> 

The radio script would not be published until [[1995]] as ''The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization,'' but this deleted scene nevertheless has much in common with a short narrative called "[[Running the Gauntlet]]," written by [[Michael Stern]] for the [[1989]] [[West End Games]] [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game|roleplaying]] sourcebook ''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]''. In that story, narrated by Wedge Antilles, Antilles and Hobbie respectively fly an X-wing and Y-wing to escort a transport past a blockading Star Destroyer using a diversionary tactic called the Tallon split.<ref name="Running the Gauntlet-GG3-1">{{WEGCite|story=Running the Gauntlet|book=Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back}}</ref> The maneuver closely parallels Skywalker's maneuver in the radio script,<ref name="ESB radio script" /> but Wedge replaces Luke as the leader, while Hobbie fills in as his wingman. The transport's pilot is only identified as an unnamed [[Captain/Legends|captain]].<ref name="Running the Gauntlet-GG3-1" /> 

These three differing versions of the events - the radio script,<ref name="ESB radio script" /> radio episode,<ref name="ESB radio" /> and story by Stern<ref name="Running the Gauntlet-GG3-1" /> - began a long history of [[Canon|continuity]] inconsistencies and revisions regarding ''Thon's Orchard''.<ref name="Insider 146" /><ref name="GG3, 2nd" /><ref name="Essential Guide to Characters" /><ref name="Isard's Revenge" /><ref name="Inside the Worlds">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref>

[[File:TarrinDatch-ESB.png|thumb|left|235px|Rogue Group pilot Tarrin Datch piloted ''Thon's Orchard'' past the Imperial blockade of Hoth.]]
The 1995 reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'', authored by [[Andy Mangels]], makes an effort to reconcile these inconsistent sources. Mangels explains how Skywalker, Antilles, and Y-wing pilot Janson escort one of the last transports, piloted by Tarrin, from Echo Base: Antilles and Janson employ the Tallon split maneuver, in conjunction with Skywalker's surprise attack from below the transport, to allow all parties to escape the Star Destroyer.<ref name="Essential Guide to Characters" /> Mangels' version favors the radio drama script over the final radio episode and effectively identifies Tarrin as the unnamed transport pilot from "Running the Gauntlet."<ref name="ESB radio" /><ref name="Essential Guide to Characters" /><ref name="Running the Gauntlet-GG3-1" /><ref name="ESB radio script" /> However, ''The Essential Guide to Characters'' created a new inconsistency by identifying the Y-wing pilot as Janson rather than Hobbie.<ref name="Essential Guide to Characters" />

In revising and expanding Stern's original ''Galaxy Guide 3'' text for the sourcebook's [[1996]] updated [[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|second edition]], author [[Pablo Hidalgo]] altered "Running the Gauntlet"{{'s}} text to identify the transport captain as Tarrin,<ref name="GG3, 2nd" /> which matched Mangels' ''The Essential Guide to Characters''.<ref name="Essential Guide to Characters" /> Hidalgo also first named the transport ''Thon's Orchard'' and identified it as the ship that was to be [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa's]] escape transport from ''The Empire Strikes Back''.<ref name="GG3, 2nd" /> This corresponds with another scene in the radio drama in which Luke, before the battle, tells Leia that he has been assigned to escort her transport<ref name="Fire and Ice">{{ESBRadio|Fire and Ice}}</ref> - though the drama is not totally consistent, since in anther scene, when Han Solo comms her transport, the voice that responds is a different character from Tarrin.<ref name="ESB radio script" /> Author [[M. Shayne Bell]]'s subsequent 1996 short story "[[Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM]]" in the anthology book ''[[Tales of the Bounty Hunters]]'' introduced a new inconsistency, identifying the princess's transport as the ''Bright Hope''.<ref name="Of Possible Futures" /> To date, the ''Bright Hope'' has remained Organa's intended transport.<ref name="Behind the Magic">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'' remains the most recent source to confirm that the [[Bright Hope/Legends|''Bright Hope'']] was [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa's]] intended escape [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|transport]] in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]. No source since has addressed the matter.</ref>

Author [[Michael A. Stackpole|Michael Stackpole's]] [[1999]] novel, ''[[X-Wing: Isard's Revenge]]'', created a new line of continuity that disregarded ''Thon's Orchard''<ref name="Isard's Revenge" /> and persisted for nearly fifteen years.<ref name="Insider 146" /> In dialogue between Antilles and [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Areta Bell]], ''Isard's Revenge'' establishes that Tarrin piloted the transport ''Dutyfree'' during the Hoth evacuation, with Bell as the transport's [[Navigator/Legends|navigator]], while Skywalker and Antilles flew escort.<ref name="Isard's Revenge" />

The [[2004]] reference book ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]'', written by [[James Luceno]], made strides toward reconciling the previous sources. Luceno's book definitively identifies ''Thon's Orchard'', ''Dutyfree'', and the ''Bright Hope'' as separate transports stationed at Echo Base during the Battle of Hoth. ''Inside the Worlds'' also designates the ''Dutyfree'' as being escorted by Skywalker and Antilles, and the ''Bright Hope'' as being escorted by Antilles, Hobbie, and Janson. However, the text does not mention Tarrin or provide any additional details for ''Thon's Orchard''.<ref name="Inside the Worlds" />

''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' of [[2008]], compiled primarily by author [[Stephen J. Sansweet]],<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> reinforced the ''Isard's Revenge'' version of events by stating that Tarrin piloted the ''Dutyfree''<ref name="CSWE-Tarrin">{{CSWECite|I|173|Datch, Tarrin}}</ref> and that Areta Bell commanded the transport as its captain during the Hoth evacuation.<ref name="CSWE-Dutyfree">{{CSWECite|I|219|''Dutyfree''}}</ref> The text makes no mention of ''Thon's Orchard''.<ref name="CSWE" /> However, the [[2013]] [[Rogues Gallery (department)|''Rogues Gallery'']] department from [[Star Wars Insider 146|''Star Wars Insider'' 146]] effectively returned the line of continuity to its original version, stating that Tarrin piloted ''Thon's Orchard'' past the Imperial blockade. To date, ''Star Wars Insider'' 146 remains the most recent source to address the matter.<ref name="Insider 146" />

===Continuity resolution===
Despite the many competing versions of the events, this article considers ''Thon's Orchard''{{'s}} continuity resolved on the basis of the ''Star Wars Insider'' 146 ''Rogues Gallery'' department. Its information was directly approved by [[Leland Chee]],<ref name="Insider 146" /> Keeper of the Holocron for the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]], which determines all ''[[Star Wars]]'' canon.<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|HolocronKeeper|status/420071186232385536|[[Leland Chee]]|date=2014-01-05|quote=@pauldunahoo @rwknopp Star Wars Canon is now determined by the Lucasfilm Story Group which @infinata and I are both a part of.|archivedate=20140112022559|nolive=1}} {{C|In response to: @rwknopp …erases the canon. Also, George Lucas does not have the ability to define how canon is treated. (@HolocronKeeper does)}}</ref> Given Chee's authority, this article concludes that Tarrin Datch piloted ''Thon's Orchard'' and that contrary claims from ''Isard's Revenge'' and ''The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia'' are in error. Moreover, this article considers ''The Essential Guide to Characters'' and ''Galaxy Guide 3'', Second Edition to be the canonical version of events for ''Thon's Orchard''{{'s}} blockade run, and considers any contradicting elements from ''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio drama or its script to be overridden.

[[File:Bright_Hope-TCG_Escape_from_Hoth.jpg|thumb|right|325px|The ''Bright Hope'' evacuates Echo Base with other transports, according to a ''Star Wars: The Card Game'' illustration.]]
This article also attempts to reconcile the multitude of sources with varying versions of Rebel pilots escorting transports, and considers the following pieces of information to be canon: Skywalker, Antilles, and Janson escort ''Thon's Orchard'', according to ''The Essential Guide to Characters'';<ref name="Essential Guide to Characters" /> Antilles and Hobbie escort ''Thon's Orchard'', with Janson riding in Hobbie's Y-wing, according to ''Galaxy Guide 3'', Second Edition;<ref name="Running the Gauntlet-GG3-2" /> Skywalker and Antilles escort the ''Dutyfree'', according to ''Isard's Revenge'' and ''Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy'';<ref name="Isard's Revenge" /> and Antilles, Hobbie, and Janson escort the ''Bright Hope'', according to ''Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy''.<ref name="Inside the Worlds" /> This article treats these escort roles as overlapping pieces between transports. In addition, this article considers Hobbie and Janson flying in a single Y-wing from ''Galaxy Guide 3'' to be the canon version of events, given that ''Galaxy Guide 3'' is the most recent source to specify a starfighter type for either character's blockade run.

Regarding the transports, ''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio drama establishes that Skywalker, Antilles, and ''Thon's Orchard'' are part of the final evacuation group;<ref name="ESB radio" /> ''Galaxy Guide 3'' confirms that ''Thon's Orchard'' is one of the last transports to evacuate;<ref name="GG3, 2nd" /> and ''Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy'' confirms both that the ''Dutyfree'' is one of the last transports to evacuate and that the ''Bright Hope'' is the final one. In addition, the ''Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy'' Echo Base map depicts ''Thon's Orchard'', ''Dutyfree'', and the ''Bright Hope'' positioned adjacently in the Echo Base hangar prior to evacuation during the Battle of Hoth, clearly suggesting that they are, indeed, the last three transports to evacuate.<ref name="Inside the Worlds" /> Therefore, given the aforementioned overlapping escort roles, this article concludes that the final evacuation group must consist of the transports ''Thon's Orchard'', ''Dutyfree'', and ''Bright Hope'', escorted collectively by Skywalker, Antilles, Hobbie, Janson, and Tarn Mison, the last following the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]].<ref name="CCG" />

This conclusion is supported by several pieces of indirect source material, the most significant of which is the [[2003]] [[Wikipedia:Nintendo GameCube|Nintendo]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''. In this game's "Battlefield Hoth" level, the player, as Luke Skywalker, and assisted by other [[Wikipedia:Non-player character|NPC]] X-wing pilots, must escort the last three transports to leave Echo Base, and these three transports leave at the same time. Although the transports are not named in the game,<ref name="Rogue Squadron III" /> they correspond to ''Thon's Orchard'', ''Dutyfree'', and the ''Bright Hope'', according to ''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio drama,<ref name="ESB radio" /> ''Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy'',<ref name="Inside the Worlds" /> and the aforementioned escort combinations, and this article therefore treats them as such. Secondly, ''The Empire Strikes Back'' establishes that the Rebel evacuation transports initially lifted off individually but were forced to begin departing in pairs as the battle progressed.<ref name="CSWE-Hoth" /><ref name="ESB" /> Thirdly, the [http://www.cardgamedb.com/index.php/starwars/star-wars-card-spoilers/_/the-hoth-cycle/escape-from-hoth/bright-hope-escape-from-hoth-65-4 "''Bright Hope''" card] from the 2013 ''[[Escape from Hoth]]'' expansion pack of ''[[Star Wars: The Card Game]]'' depicts the ''Bright Hope'' departing Echo Base with other transports as a group.<ref name="Escape from Hoth">{{FFGTCG|set=Escape from Hoth|cardname=''Bright Hope''|link=the-hoth-cycle/escape-from-hoth/bright-hope-escape-from-hoth-65-4}}</ref> Finally, ''Tales of the Bounty Hunters'' establishes that the ''Bright Hope'' was escorted by six X-wing fighters,<ref name="Of Possible Futures" /> which this article treats as applying to all three transports of the final evacuation group.
